specMark.why: T3-565 adds wakes (a child that ended without reporting still wakes its parent) and removes none; a finished child's result is still delivered.
T3-565 adds a wake for a command whose process or session is gone; a command that ends still wakes its thread.

T3-567 lets a slow watch park, so the thread leaves Working, but the wake on the event is kept; T3-565 makes a landing always wake its thread and stops a watch on a Forge item waiting only on Henry from counting as a machine wait.

T3-567 turns a one-off check-back bound to its thread into a time-parked wait and has agents park on the event when T3 can see it, so a check-back that fires although T3 could see the event goes; repeating, webhook and fresh-session routines stay.
Neither Spec touches the unattended nudge or the context-rollover notices; they are not wakes an agent asked for.
